page: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-384GB is a Premium family cloud server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 500 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier CPU performance. The stress-ng single-core score of 3887.38 and multi-core score of 166533.72 both rank in the top 10% tier. PassMark CPU testing confirms this standing with a score of 95708.23 and an extended instructions score of 117767.85, both in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression at 40.67 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.15 GB/sec single-threaded and 655.33 GB/sec multi-threaded also place in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is top-tier at 8129.22 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths perform in the average tier at 178.6 GB/sec and 78.06 GB/sec respectively.

This server is well-suited for highly parallelized workloads, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference. PassMark database operations scored in the top 25% at 29253.45, supported by a strong Redis SET performance of 102.43 million operations per second. For AI workloads, prompt processing for a 135M parameter LLM model reaches a top-tier 4527.08 tokens per second, while a 7B model processes prompts at 221.55 tokens per second. Given the high physical core density and substantial memory capacity, this instance offers high resource density for enterprise applications, though the shared CPU allocation model represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, isolated CPU performance.
